notes: Video design and reading-time rules for Remaining Action, read by templates/manim/reading_model.py (scenes hold text automatically), tools/video/check_design.py and tools/video/check_reading.py (gates). Every constant is a tunable default; 'sources' says where each one comes from. Edit this file yourself: Claude may not. The semantic palette was changed in 2026-10 to stay distinguishable for colour-blind viewers (the former colours are listed under 'former'; the source explainer's figures still use them).

palette.background_note: The video background: read by templates/manim/common.py (BG, config.background_color), tools/video/thumbnail.py, tools/video/assemble.py (padding) and tools/video/check_design.py. Keep every semantic colour at 4.5:1 or more against it (tests/test_video_design.py checks).

semantic.#2dd4bf: green: holds, stable, verified (teal-green, told apart from red by deuteranopes)
semantic.#fbbf24: amber: contrast case, unstable, second option
semantic.#818cf8: blue: reference case, first option (indigo, told apart from green by tritanopes)
semantic.#ef4444: red: failure or violation, always with a text label

former.#f87171: red until 2026-10 (indistinguishable from the green for deuteranopes: CIEDE2000 1.9)

sources.action_safe_inset, graphics_safe_inset: EBU R 95, safe areas for 16:9 television production: action-safe 93 %, graphics-safe 90 % of the picture. YouTube has no overscan, but the player's controls and captions cover the edges.
sources.min_cap_px_*: Tunable default. Reasoning: on a phone held in landscape about 30 cm away the picture is about 7 cm tall; a cap height of 22 px in 1080 lines is then about 1.4 mm, an x-height of about 1 mm, or 0.2 degrees: the lower end of the fluent reading range (about 0.2 to 2 degrees of x-height) in Legge and Bigelow (2011), Journal of Vision 11(5):8. The house rule 'font size 24 or more at 1080p' gives a 33 px cap height for Text and 23 px for MathTex.
sources.contrast_*: WCAG 2.x contrast ratio: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (success criterion 1.4.3).
sources.cvd_*: Colour-vision deficiency simulation with the Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009) matrices at full severity, colour difference CIEDE2000. Thresholds are tunable defaults: below 5 two colours read as the same, below 12 they need a text label or a different shape as well.
sources.max_elements_*, max_text_items_*: Tunable defaults against clutter (one idea per scene).
sources.thumbnail_small: 168 x 94 px, the small thumbnail size in YouTube's suggested-video lists.
sources.text_wpm: Tunable default below the 238 words per minute average silent reading rate of adults for non-fiction (Brysbaert 2019, Journal of Memory and Language 109:104047), because viewers read while they listen and the text is technical.
sources.equation_*: House rule from the episode plan: hold every new equation 2 to 3 s before speaking over it; per-term time is a tunable default.
sources.narration_factor, narration_overlap: Tunable default: reading while the narration says something else takes longer.
sources.min_display_s: Tunable default for any label; subtitle guidelines use a similar floor (for example, about 5/6 s minimum per subtitle event in Netflix's timed-text style guide).
sources.narration_wpm_*: House pacing rule (130 to 150 spoken words per minute); warning and error thresholds are tunable defaults.
sources.checked: EBU R 95, Brysbaert 2019, Legge and Bigelow 2011 and the Netflix minimum duration were checked against their publishers' pages on 2026-10-30; WCAG and Machado et al. are cited from the standard texts.
sources.equation_numbers: House rule (2026-10, the channel owner): a viewer never looks an equation up by its tag, so the video carries no equation labels; false rejects all of them, true allows only the video's own numbering, (1), (2), ... in order of first appearance, never the explainer's numbers. Checked by tools/video/check_selfcontained.py.
sources.self_contained: House rule (2026-10, the channel owner): the video assumes that nothing exists besides itself: no reference to the explainer, code, files, links or a document's numbering on screen, in narration, captions or chapters. 'allow' lists regular expressions removed before matching (robotics 'link' usage). Mentions of other episodes of the series (by title or meaning; the words episode, series, previously, next time) are not flagged; another episode's equation numbers always are. Tunable.
sources.recall: Recall load (design warning, never an error, tools/video/check_reading.py): a callback to an equation that is no longer on screen asks the viewer to hold it in memory; working memory holds few items and decays within tens of seconds without rehearsal (Cowan 2001, Behavioral and Brain Sciences 24:87; Peterson and Peterson 1959, Journal of Experimental Psychology 58:193). window_s and max_callbacks are tunable defaults.
sources.min_gap_*: Tunable defaults: 0.15 Manim units is about 20 px at 1080p, the smallest gap that keeps two labels visibly separate on a phone; below 0.05 (about 7 px) they read as one block. The same two thresholds apply between a text and any strong stroke (a curve, an arrow, a plot line, an outline; strong_stroke_width and strong_stroke_contrast decide, so faint grid lines do not count). A label made with templates/manim/common.py attach() is exempt from the strokes of the object it labels; the crossing rule still applies.
sources.thumbnail_*: thumbnail_title_shade is the opacity of the uniform dark panel under the thumbnail title (0.96: labels left in the frame there fade to near invisibility instead of reading as clutter around the title); the busy thresholds are the edge density (share of pixels with a strong local gradient) and the standard deviation of luminance (0-255) behind the title after the panel: tunable defaults.
sources.numbers: House rule (2026-10, the channel owner): numbers read the way a person writes them: 2-3 significant digits for readouts, no trailing zeros (0.500000 becomes 0.5), exact values shown exactly ('0', 'exactly 0', '½'), one quantity at one precision within a scene, a real minus sign, a space before a unit. templates/manim/common.py fmt() formats them; tools/video/check_numbers.py checks the layout logs (live readouts sampled over time), narration, captions, chapters and thumbnail. Digit counts and the comparison tolerance are tunable defaults.
sources.space_*: Tunable defaults for the space-usage warnings (check_design.py, settled frames): coverage of the graphics-safe area by content boxes on a 48 x 27 grid, the centre of mass of that content (0 = centred, 1 = at the edge), the largest empty rectangle while content crowds the rest, and the extent of the content's bounding box. Composition guidance, not a standard: warnings only.
sources.motion_*: Tunable defaults for the checks during animations (check_design.py, from the probe's 15 fps timeline): two opaque texts overlapping while something moves (warning from 0.25 s, error from 1.5 s), and a live readout whose width changes by more than readout_width_jitter_warn units (about 16 px at 1080p) while it updates.
sources.series: The owner's decisions (2026-10), after the 3Blue1Brown pattern: speech from 0 s with the hook, no channel card; the spoken series context at the first natural break (about 30-90 s) over a 4-6 s builds-on frame; recaps of what the episode uses, marked and with their own chapter; a 15-20 s outro with the takeaway card, the channel name and the teaser, the right ~40 % of the frame (x > 1.4 Manim units) empty for YouTube's end-screen elements (which show in the last 5-20 s of a video). tools/video/check_series.py warns; the reviewers judge.
sources.align_*: Tunable defaults for the alignment warnings (check_design.py, settled frames), added 2026-10-31 after a legend whose tags were staggered by 0.51 units passed every check: three or more texts of one kind and size stacked within align_stack_gap of each other (a column), or side by side with heights within align_row_height_ratio (a row), warn when their left edges, centres or right edges (rows: centres or bottoms) are all within align_max but none within align_tol (about 4 px at 1080p), or when all but one align and the odd one is off by less than align_outlier_max. A larger offset reads as a deliberate indent. Warnings only; legend_table() in common.py aligns by construction.
sources.panel_*: Tunable defaults for the panel-balance warnings (check_design.py, settled frames), added 2026-10-31: content split by an empty vertical gutter of at least panel_gutter_min units (titles in the top panel_header_band are ignored) forms side-by-side panels of at least panel_min_width of the safe width. A warning when their content bottoms differ by more than panel_bottom_diff_warn while their centres differ by more than panel_centre_diff_warn (one side ends much higher; a short column centred beside a tall picture is fine), or when a panel's largest empty block is more than panel_empty_warn of its area. The outro is exempt (it keeps the end-screen area empty). Warnings only.
